title: Zenoh transport: session mapping, pub/sub, and type containment
milestone: M5 — Stage 4: Adapters and Zenoh transport
body:
## Outcome
The reference transport implementing the frozen contract: private key-expression mapping and message publish/subscribe.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Passes the transport contract suite unchanged from the in-memory transport
- [ ] Zenoh types never appear in a public signature; enforced by the CI lint, not by review
- [ ] Only the stable `zenoh` and `zenoh-ext` API surface is used; any `unstable` feature is named and justified
- [ ] Opaque session ids do not yield guessable public addresses

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-zenoh`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Zenoh presence via liveliness tokens
milestone: M5 — Stage 4: Adapters and Zenoh transport
body:
## Outcome
Neutral presence mapped onto liveliness tokens with history-capable liveliness subscribers.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A newly started peer learns about sessions that were already online
- [ ] Session exit produces `unreachable` within a stated bound
- [ ] Ambiguous states surface as `unknown` rather than a guess
- [ ] No Zenoh concept leaks into `PresenceRecord`

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-zenoh`

title: Zenoh local-mode and LAN-mode security configuration
milestone: M5 — Stage 4: Adapters and Zenoh transport
body:
## Outcome
Local mode bound to loopback with no manual certificate management, and LAN mode with authenticated encryption and pairing-issued certificates.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Local mode exposes nothing beyond the host by default
- [ ] Multicast scouting behaviour matches the C7 decision and can be disabled
- [ ] LAN mode uses TLS or QUIC; ACL subjects are authenticated ones only, never `zid`
- [ ] Envelope signatures remain the authenticity proof; transport security is never treated as a substitute
- [ ] The G3 fallback (fixed local endpoint, scouting off) is reachable by configuration

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-zenoh`, `oac-security-work`

title: Claude adapter: channel server, legacy negotiation, inbound delivery
milestone: M5 — Stage 4: Adapters and Zenoh transport
body:
## Outcome
The production Claude adapter: an MCP server declaring `capabilities.experimental["claude/channel"]`, negotiating a legacy revision, and delivering `notifications/claude/channel` into the addressed live session.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Passes the adapter contract suite against the fake, then against real Claude Code behind the opt-in tier
- [ ] Provenance arrives as identifier-safe `meta` attributes per the C6 decision
- [ ] A resolved notification send is reported as 'handed to harness', never as 'seen by the model'
- [ ] Mid-turn sends behave correctly under the queue-then-deliver-in-order rule
- [ ] Permission relay is off by default
- [ ] No inbox polling anywhere in the adapter

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-claude-channels`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Claude adapter: outbound tools and session registration
milestone: M5 — Stage 4: Adapters and Zenoh transport
body:
## Outcome
Outbound MCP tools (`send`, `reply`, `list_sessions`, `whoami`) and session registration that captures the live `session_id` through the supported hook surface.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `session_id` captured from hook input (for example `SessionStart`), not from an undocumented environment variable
- [ ] Reply correlation works through the `meta` attributes the server asks the model to echo back, and tolerates the model omitting them
- [ ] Tool results never assert delivery the provider did not confirm
- [ ] Registration and deregistration are correct across session start and exit, and across `--resume` per the B2 finding

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-claude-channels`

title: Codex adapter: app-server client and thread/turn mapping
milestone: M5 — Stage 4: Adapters and Zenoh transport
body:
## Outcome
The Codex adapter's client half: JSON-RPC over the chosen transport, thread and turn mapping onto neutral sessions and messages, and event translation.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Uses the checked-in schema artifacts as the source of truth for message shapes
- [ ] `item/completed` treated as authoritative; deltas are not
- [ ] Thread ids mapped to neutral session ids without exposing them publicly
- [ ] The adapter never calls the OpenAI model API and never handles `auth.json` or keyring credentials
- [ ] Experimental methods are isolated behind a named compatibility shim pinned to a version

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-codex-appserver`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Codex adapter: live inbound injection with the documented fallback
milestone: M5 — Stage 4: Adapters and Zenoh transport
body:
## Outcome
Inbound delivery into a live thread via `thread/queue/add` or `turn/start` through the shared daemon, with the OAC-owned app-server plus `codex --remote` fallback if the G2 primary path failed.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Whichever path G2 passed is implemented; the other is either implemented or explicitly deferred with a reason
- [ ] Inbound framing puts a machine-generated provenance header outside a delimited untrusted body
- [ ] `turn/steer` is either unused or gated behind an explicit authorization check, because unauthorized steer is a code-execution risk
- [ ] No rollout-file reading or writing anywhere
- [ ] No inbox polling; event subscription only

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-codex-appserver`, `oac-security-work`

title: Codex adapter: outbound tool surface and reply correlation
milestone: M5 — Stage 4: Adapters and Zenoh transport
body:
## Outcome
Outbound sends from a Codex session through OAC tools registered with `codex mcp add`, with correlation that works without a channel-tag convention.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The OAC MCP server is reachable as a Codex tool provider on the pinned version
- [ ] Correlation mechanism from the C9 decision implemented and tested against a reply that omits the correlation hint
- [ ] Tool surface matches the Claude side: `send`, `reply`, `list_sessions`, `whoami`
- [ ] Nothing depends on the deleted `codex mcp-server` surface

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-codex-appserver`

title: Daemon, MCP shims, and authenticated local IPC
milestone: M5 — Stage 4: Adapters and Zenoh transport
body:
## Outcome
The process model from C2 realized: the long-lived component holding identity, policy, transport, and provider clients, plus whatever shim the harnesses spawn.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Local IPC authenticates the peer process — Windows named-pipe security descriptors, Unix socket permissions
- [ ] Key material lives in one process only
- [ ] A shim crash does not take down presence for other sessions
- [ ] Clean shutdown deregisters presence
- [ ] Startup is idempotent; a second `oac start` does not create a second peer

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-security-work`

title: CLI: start, status, sessions, doctor, and zero-file defaults
milestone: M5 — Stage 4: Adapters and Zenoh transport
body:
**Source:** DESIGN CLI; PLANNING-PROMPT §5.11

## Outcome
The user-facing CLI, working with no configuration file on a clean machine.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `oac start` works with no config file present
- [ ] `oac sessions` lists reachable sessions with harness, capabilities, and whether active inbound is supported
- [ ] `oac doctor` diagnoses the common failures: wrong MCP revision negotiated, no daemon, scouting blocked, pairing missing, credential store unavailable
- [ ] No Docker, Kubernetes, cloud account, or separately administered server is required
- [ ] Exit codes and machine-readable output defined for scripting

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`

title: Document and script the OAC-enabled launch for each harness
milestone: M5 — Stage 4: Adapters and Zenoh transport
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.9; ADR-001-A2

## Outcome
One documented command each to launch Claude Code and Codex OAC-enabled, since neither harness can attach a channel to an already-running session.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Claude command quoted verbatim including `--channels` and, until OAC is allowlisted, `--dangerously-load-development-channels`
- [ ] The interactive confirmation is presented as a feature, not bypassed or automated away
- [ ] Codex command reflects whichever G2 path shipped
- [ ] Distribution constraints stated: the Anthropic allowlist, org `allowedChannelPlugins` and `channelsEnabled`, and no availability on Bedrock, Vertex, or Foundry
- [ ] Failure modes have a matching `oac doctor` check

**Skills:** `oac-claude-channels`, `oac-codex-appserver`, `oac-release`

title: End-to-end test: Claude to Codex and back, no receiver polling
milestone: M6 — Stage 5: End-to-end and threat verification
body:
**Source:** ADR-001 Validation criterion; DESIGN Testing

## Outcome
The validation criterion executed for real: Claude -> OAC -> Zenoh -> Codex -> Zenoh -> OAC -> Claude.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A live Claude Code session, launched OAC-enabled, sends to a live Codex session and the Codex model answers without any receiver-side polling
- [ ] Codex replies actively and Claude receives it as a channel wake
- [ ] Neither side invokes nor holds credentials for the other's model API, asserted by the test, not by inspection
- [ ] Sender identity and authorization are enforced rather than inferred from content
- [ ] Runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux on the pinned provider versions

**Skills:** `oac-testing`, `oac-gates`

title: Security verification: spoofing, replay, duplicates, unauthorized routing
milestone: M6 — Stage 5: End-to-end and threat verification
body:
**Source:** DESIGN Testing; PLANNING-PROMPT §7

## Outcome
The security suite re-run against the real transport and real adapters, not just the fakes.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Impersonation attempt over real Zenoh is rejected at signature verification
- [ ] Replay and duplicate handling produce the specified delivery states end to end
- [ ] An unauthorized peer can neither discover nor address a session
- [ ] A session in one working directory is not discoverable by a peer not authorized for it
- [ ] Permission relay is confirmed off, and the consequence of enabling it is documented
- [ ] Unauthorized `turn/steer` is proven impossible or proven gated

**Skills:** `oac-testing`, `oac-security-work`

title: Resilience: disconnect, reconnect, restart, and expiry
milestone: M6 — Stage 5: End-to-end and threat verification
body:
## Outcome
Behaviour under network and process churn, with no promise of exactly-once delivery.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Peer disconnect and reconnect restores presence without duplicate delivery
- [ ] Daemon restart preserves device identity and re-registers live sessions
- [ ] TTL expiry produces `expired`, not silent loss
- [ ] Messages to a session that exited mid-flight produce `unreachable`
- [ ] Duplicate suppression holds across restart

**Skills:** `oac-testing`

title: Cross-platform CLI smoke tests
milestone: M6 — Stage 5: End-to-end and threat verification
body:
## Outcome
A clean-machine smoke run on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## Acceptance
- [ ] One-command local startup from a fresh install with no config file (DESIGN acceptance criterion 1)
- [ ] `status`, `sessions`, and `doctor` behave correctly with zero, one, and two sessions
- [ ] Credential-store path exercised on each platform, plus the encrypted-file fallback on headless Linux
- [ ] Clean shutdown leaves no orphaned process or stale presence

**Skills:** `oac-testing`

title: Map DESIGN acceptance criteria 1-10 and every threat mitigation to a passing test
milestone: M6 — Stage 5: End-to-end and threat verification
body:
**Source:** DESIGN v0.1 acceptance criteria; PLANNING-PROMPT §11.2

## Outcome
A traceability table: criterion or threat -> named test -> current result.

## Acceptance
- [ ] All ten DESIGN acceptance criteria map to a named passing test
- [ ] Every threat-table mitigation names the test that proves it, and that test passes
- [ ] Criterion 9 (Zenoh types confined) is proven by the CI lint, not by assertion
- [ ] Criterion 10 (transport contract documented well enough for a second backend) is evidenced by E9
- [ ] Any unproven criterion is called out as a v0.1 gap rather than quietly marked done

**Skills:** `oac-testing`, `oac-security-work`

title: User and contributor documentation
milestone: M7 — Stage 6: Release hygiene
body:
## Outcome
README, install and launch guides per harness, the security model in user terms, and a contributor guide pointing at the skill tree.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A new user gets two harnesses talking by following the docs alone
- [ ] The untrusted-peer-content warning is prominent, not a footnote
- [ ] The research-preview status of both provider surfaces is stated with pinned versions
- [ ] Contributor guide routes work-item labels to the skills that cover them

**Skills:** `oac-release`

title: License inventory and third-party audit
milestone: M7 — Stage 6: Release hygiene
body:
## Outcome
A complete dependency inventory with licenses, and a CI check that fails on an unapproved one.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Every dependency: name, version, license, why it is needed
- [ ] Copyleft flagged; Apache-2.0 compatibility confirmed for the shipped artifact
- [ ] Zenoh's dual EPL-2.0 / Apache-2.0 position recorded explicitly
- [ ] Reused Codex crates recorded with their Apache-2.0 provenance
- [ ] NOTICE file generated and current

**Skills:** `oac-release`, `oac-evidence`

title: Release packaging for Windows, macOS, and Linux
milestone: M7 — Stage 6: Release hygiene
body:
## Outcome
Reproducible single-binary artifacts per platform with checksums.

## Acceptance
- [ ] One binary per platform, no runtime install required
- [ ] Windows MSVC and GNU targets addressed explicitly
- [ ] Checksums and provenance published with the release
- [ ] Actual binary size recorded against the estimate
- [ ] The release runs the full CI-default tier plus the opt-in provider tier before publishing

**Skills:** `oac-release`

title: Publish the deferred-work list, known risks, and preview upgrade notes
milestone: M7 — Stage 6: Release hygiene
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §8 Stage 6, §9.12, §9.13

## Outcome
Shipped versions of the deferred list and the risk list, plus upgrade notes for the provider preview surfaces.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Every ADR non-goal and v0.1 exclusion restated as an explicit 'not in v0.1' with its reason
- [ ] Known risks carry an early-warning signal and a response
- [ ] Upgrade notes state which gates must be re-run when Claude Code or Codex moves, and where the pins live
- [ ] Any UNVERIFIED item still open at release is listed, not quietly dropped

**Skills:** `oac-release`, `oac-evidence`

title: Write the Tier 0 router: CLAUDE.md and the `oac` entry skill
milestone: M8 — Agent enablement
body:
**Source:** `docs/planning/SKILLS-MODEL.md`

## Outcome
The always-loaded layer: a short `CLAUDE.md` and an `oac` router skill that names the current stage and routes a work item to the right skills.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` is under 40 lines: what OAC is, the inviolable boundaries in one list, where the plan lives, and how to find the right skill
- [ ] The router maps every work-item label to the skills that cover it
- [ ] The router reads current stage and gate status from a single status file rather than restating it
- [ ] Nothing in Tier 0 duplicates content that lives in a skill body

**Skills:** `oac-authoring-skills`

title: Write the guardrail skills: `oac-boundaries` and `oac-evidence`
milestone: M8 — Agent enablement
body:
## Outcome
The two skills nearly every task loads: the ADR boundary self-check, and the evidence standard.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `oac-boundaries` lists every ADR-001 MUST NOT with a concrete example of drifting into it, plus the grep and lint commands that catch the mechanical violations
- [ ] `oac-evidence` states the first-party-source rule, the URL + version + retrieval-date requirement, verbatim API naming, and UNVERIFIED labelling, with the Appendix B source index as a reference file
- [ ] Each SKILL.md body stays under 200 lines; detail moves to `references/`
- [ ] Descriptions are trigger-rich so the router does not have to explain when to load them

**Skills:** `oac-authoring-skills`

title: Write the stage skills: planning-package, gates, spec-authoring, implementation, security, testing, release
milestone: M8 — Agent enablement
body:
## Outcome
One procedural skill per stage, loaded only while working in that stage.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Seven skills: `oac-planning-package`, `oac-gates`, `oac-spec-authoring`, `oac-implementation`, `oac-security-work`, `oac-testing`, `oac-release`
- [ ] Each carries the checklists and templates its stage needs, not background theory
- [ ] `oac-gates` ships a gate-result template and one reference file per gate
- [ ] Each states its exit criteria so an agent can tell when the work item is done
- [ ] No stage skill repeats the guardrail content; it links instead

**Skills:** `oac-authoring-skills`

title: Write the surface reference skills: Claude Channels, Codex app-server, MCP, Zenoh
milestone: M8 — Agent enablement
body:
## Outcome
Four reference skills holding the expensive, version-pinned protocol detail, loaded only when touching that surface.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `oac-claude-channels`, `oac-codex-appserver`, `oac-mcp`, `oac-zenoh`
- [ ] Every fact carries its first-party source, pinned version, and retrieval date
- [ ] Method names, capability keys, flags, and paths quoted verbatim
- [ ] Each names the constraints that most often trip an agent up — the legacy MCP negotiation requirement, the no-attach-to-running-session rule, Zenoh >= 1.10.0 for loopback discovery, and `zid` not being an identity
- [ ] Each declares the pin it was written against so a version bump visibly invalidates it

**Skills:** `oac-authoring-skills`, `oac-evidence`
